attributes.morphology: nanoscale precipitates with Moiré fringes and coffee-bean contrast
attributes.composition: almost entirely Cr with negligible Nb

evidence.quote: In PA samples, alongside the tens-to-hundreds-nanometer Cr2Nb particles (red arrows in Fig. 5a–b), a profusion of nanoscale precipitates appeared (green circles in Fig. 5c). Many of these particles exhibited Moiré fringes and “coffee-bean” contrast [26], indicating closely matched lattice parameters between precipitate and Cu matrix. PSD analysis (Fig. 5d) revealed a bimodal distribution: the nano-precipitates averaged 4.9 nm, while the Cr2Nb particles averaged 42.3 nm. EDS mapping (Fig. 5e and f) and the point spectrum from Spot 1 showed that the nanoscale phase consisted almost entirely of Cr, with negligible Nb.

evidence.section: 4.2. Aging-induced strengthening mechanisms and conductivity enhancement
evidence.quote: The calculation results revealed that the yield strength of the Cu-Cr-Nb in AB state was mainly dependent on dislocation and dispersion strengthening.

Quantitative strengthening calculations demonstrated that, in addition to the retained dispersion strengthening and dislocation hardening from Cr2Nb, significant Cr precipitation contributed to the overall strength.
Furthermore, hetero-deformation-induced back stresses enhanced the work-hardening rate.
